name: Yamaha TG55
source: Yamaha TG55 Owner's Manual, part 2 (TG55E_2.PDF, www2.yamaha.co.jp/manual/pdf/emi/english/synth/TG55E_2.PDF; cached at midimanuals.com), appendix 'MIDI DATA FORMAT' Add-1..Add-20: (3-1-4) program change normal/direct, (3-3-1) parameter change, (3-3-2) bulk dump, (3-3-3) bulk dump request, charts 1-12 (parameter tables multi/voice/drum/AWM element/effect/filter/switch remote/system/error, bulk formats voice/multi/system); utility chapter pp.104-111; part 1 (TG55E_1.PDF) preset wave list p.25 and effect list/params pp.28, 74-76. Read from 300 dpi renders of the scans. Cross-checked against Carlo Bandini's SY55-Editor (github.com/Carlobandini/SY55-Editor, source/sy55.py: identical F0 43 1n 35 addressing, n2 numbers, element/filter t2 bits, edit-buffer request) and its stored 547-byte 4AWM init-voice dump (layout, 0-based wave numbers and checksum verified by this schema's generator). Edisyn has no SY/TG55 editor (only TG33/DX/FB01/FS1R).

yamaha.deviceNumber: UTILITY > MIDI > Device# = off, 1-16, all. Messages carry n = Device# - 1 in the low nibble of the sub-status (1n / 0n / 2n). 'all' receives any n and transmits with n = 0 (device 1). 'off' = no SysEx sent or received (error 05 'MIDI Device# off'). Switch-remote messages are received regardless of device number.

paramChange.value: v1 = (value >> 7) & 7F, v2 = value & 7F -- for every param (single-byte params always have v1 = 0; 2-byte params (wave number 0-255, scaling offsets 1-255) put bit 7 in v1). 'value' is the WIRE value: apply signMag encoding first.
paramChange.element: voice params with element != null: byte 6 = pcSub | (element << 4), element 0-3 (00ee0000). pcSub already holds the filter bit for filter 2 (40h: 0fee0000). Filter-common params send f = 0.

groups.02: voice header + voice common + element enable
groups.07: AWM element (wave/pitch/pitch EG/LFO, amp EG/level scaling)

paramChange.example: element 2 (e=1) filter 1 cutoff = 100: F0 43 10 35 09 10 00 01 00 64 F7; element 2 filter 2 cutoff: F0 43 10 35 09 50 00 01 00 64 F7; element 1 wave 200 (card): F0 43 10 35 07 00 00 01 01 48 F7; voice volume 127: F0 43 10 35 02 00 00 22 00 7F F7
paramChange.receiveOnly: The TG55 receives parameter changes but transmits only ERROR INFORMATION (group 7F); front-panel edits are not echoed (the SY55 does echo).

bulkDump.header: 26 bytes counted from the 'L': 'LM  8103' (4C 4D 20 20 38 31 30 33) + 2 ASCII type chars ('VC' voice 56 43, 'MU' multi 4D 55, 'SY' system 53 59) + 14 x 00 (additional header, ignored on receive) + memory type + memory number
bulkDump.byteCount: 14-bit, 7 bits per byte (MSB first) = number of bytes from the 'L' through the last data byte (26-byte header + data), checksum and F7 excluded
bulkDump.checksum: 7-bit two's complement of the sum of every byte from the 'L' through the last data byte: sum = (sum of those bytes) & 7F; checksum = (128 - sum) & 7F, so (bytes + checksum) % 128 == 0. Verified on a real SY55 dump.
bulkDump.memoryNumber: voice 00-3F (I01-I64 / P01-P64), multi 00-0F; 00 for edit buffer and system

VC.layout: voice header 11 (mode, name x10) | effect 5 | voice common 21 | element data 9 x N | per element 112 x N: AWM element data 1 (27), filter 1 (29), filter 2 (29), filter common (3), AWM element data 2 (24). N = 1/2/4 from the mode byte (5/6/7). Drum set (mode 10): header 11 | effect 5 | common 21 | 61 x 9 drum key data (C1-C6, chart 3) -- not modelled.

MU.layout: multi header 11 (10 name + effect source select) | effect 5 | 16 x 9 per-channel voice data (chart 1)

dumpRequest.note: No checksum and no byte count in a request. Card memory cannot be requested.

yamaha.canonicalImage: Params' dumpOffset index a 521-byte 4-element voice image counted from the mode byte (first byte after the 26-byte header). For a dump with N elements: common area (dumpArea 'common', offsets 0-36) is identical; dumpArea 'elementData' lives at 37 + 9*e + areaOffset; dumpArea 'elementBlock' lives at 37 + 9*N + 112*e + areaOffset (for N = 4 this equals dumpOffset). Elements e >= N are absent from the dump.

encodings.msb1: 2 bytes in the dump [value >> 7, value & 7F] (MSB byte is 0-1); param change sends v1 = value >> 7, v2 = value & 7F
encodings.signMag: sign-magnitude in one byte: wire = value < 0 ? (1 << signBit) | -value : value; decode: wire & (1<<signBit) ? -(wire & ((1<<signBit)-1)) : wire. 'minus zero' (e.g. 08h / 10h) decodes to 0. Schema min/max are the SIGNED values.

system.note: System params by param change F0 43 1n 35 0F 00 00 <n2> 00 <v> F7 (not part of a voice; shown for setup automation only)

params.07: Bulk Data Memory Protect 0 off, 1 on
params.08: Program Change Mode 0 off, 1 normal, 2 direct

wavesNote: Preset ROM waveforms (TG55 Owner's Manual part 1 p.25, 'PRESET WAVE LIST'). Stored wave number = list index (0 = 001 Piano ... 73 = 074 Shaker) when Wave Source = preset (0). Values 74-255 only make sense with Wave Source = card (up to 256 waves on an AWM wave card). 59-74 (BD1..Shaker) are the drum/percussion waves.
effectTypesNote: Voice effect types 1-34 (manual part 1 p.28) with each type's three parameters (manual pp.74-76 give names and unit ranges). The raw value -> unit tables ('values', raw = index; 'max' = last valid raw value) are NOT in the Yamaha MIDI tables; they come from SY55-Editor (see uncertain). A null entry = the type has no such parameter.

params.name: Element Mode
params.note: Element select mode: 5 = 1AWM poly, 6 = 2AWM poly, 7 = 4AWM poly, 10 = DRUM SET (not editable here; memory slots 63/64 are fixed to drum sets). Changing it changes the edit-buffer dump length (1/2/4 elements); re-request the edit buffer afterwards.

params.name: Effect Type
params.note: 1-34; see top-level effectTypes for what params 1-3 mean per type. The system-wide Effect on/off lives in UTILITY (system param 09).

params.name: Effect Param 1
params.note: meaning and valid range depend on fxType: effectTypes[fxType-1].params[0] (raw value = index into its values list; max differs per type)

params.name: Effect Param 2
params.note: meaning and valid range depend on fxType: effectTypes[fxType-1].params[1] (raw value = index into its values list; max differs per type)

params.name: Effect Param 3
params.note: meaning and valid range depend on fxType: effectTypes[fxType-1].params[2] (raw value = index into its values list; max differs per type)

params.name: Aftertouch Pitch Bend Range
params.note: wire 0-12 = 0..+12, 16-28 = 0..-12 (bit 4 = sign); values here are signed semitones

params.name: Output Select
params.note: An SY55 always transmits 0 here, so a dump from an SY55 lands as stereo L/R (manual note)

params.name: AWM Wave Card ID (MSB)
params.note: card ID = MSB*128 + LSB; 0 = no wave card used, 1-16383 = card ID. Separate param changes for MSB (23h) and LSB (24h).

params.name: Element 1 Enable
params.note: Element Enable: F0 43 1n 35 02 00 00 7F 00 <0000 e3 e2 e1 e0> F7. Not in the bulk dump and not readable: the driver keeps its own byte (start 0Fh = all on) and sends the whole byte.

banks.label: voices I (internal)
banks.note: I01-I64. prog 62/63 (I63/I64) are drum sets (mode fixed at 10): read/keep them as raw syx only, never decode into the voice edit buffer, and never write a normal voice there (expect error 19 'Voice Type').

banks.label: voices P (preset)
banks.note: ROM P01-P64, readable with memory type 02 without selecting them. P63/P64 are drum sets.

banks.label: voices C (card)
banks.note: MCD32/MCD64 card (bank 1/2 chosen in UTILITY). No SysEx memory type for card: select it, then request the edit buffer.

banks.label: multis I (internal)
banks.note: Multi-play setups I01-I16 = PC 64-79. 186-byte MU dumps; raw backup/restore only.

programs.note: No bank select (CC0/32 ignored). Program change works on the VOICE receive channel. In 'normal' program change mode PC 0-63 picks a voice in whichever memory (I/P/C) is active and PC 64-79 a multi (multi mode); memory cannot be changed. In 'direct' mode (set it -- see setup) a PC of 119-127 is a prefix that takes effect with the NEXT program change: 122 = voice play mode internal, 123 = card, 124 = preset; 125/126/127 = multi play mode internal/card/preset (then PC 64-79). 119/120/121 = 'individual' internal/card/preset (changes one multi part's voice in multi mode). So programChange(bank, prog) = Cn <prefix>, Cn <prog + offset>.

backup.restore: Send the saved dumps back unchanged (memory type 00 + original number), >= 120 ms apart, with Bulk In Protect OFF. Voices before multis (multis reference voices by number).
backup.notInSysex: Card voices/multis, the sequencer demo, and element-enable state have no bulk format.

setup: Firmware/model: TG55 (rack) or SY55 -- same SysEx. The SY55 also echoes front-panel edits as parameter changes; the TG55 does not.
[UTILITY] > MIDI > Device# = 1 (the editor default; n = 0). 'all' also works. 'off' disables all SysEx.
[UTILITY] > MIDI > Receive Ch = the editor channel (voice receive channel; program changes arrive here). 'omni' also works.
[UTILITY] > MIDI > Program Change = direct, so the editor can switch between internal / preset / card memories (normal mode only steps within the current memory).
[UTILITY] > MIDI > Bulk In Protect = off -- only needed to WRITE internal memory; edit-buffer dumps are received regardless. It turns itself back ON at every power-up, so repeat each session.
Be in VOICE play mode (not MULTI, not DEMO) with a normal voice (not I63/I64/P63/P64 drum sets): voice edit-buffer dumps are received only in voice mode and no SysEx is accepted in demo mode.
Cable both ways: interface out -> TG55 MIDI IN, TG55 MIDI OUT -> interface in (dump replies and error messages need the return path).
Master volume/effect: [UTILITY] > Effect = on, or the voice effect is bypassed system-wide.
driverNotes: Yamaha SY/TG55 SysEx (manufacturer 43h). (1) DEVICE: n = Device# - 1 (default Device# 1 -> n 0); sub-status 1n = parameter change, 0n = bulk dump, 2n = dump request. Match incoming dumps on F0 43 0x 7A (any x if the unit is on 'all'; it transmits as n = 0). (2) PARAMETER CHANGE (sendParam): 11 bytes F0 43 1n 35 G S H P V1 V2 F7 with G = p.pcGroup, S = p.pcSub | (p.element << 4) for element params (p.pcSub alone for common), H = p.pcHigh (0), P = p.pcParam, wire = signMag-encoded value (p.encoding === 'signMag'), V1 = (wire >> 7) & 7F, V2 = wire & 7F. Example: element 2 filter 1 cutoff 100 -> F0 43 10 35 09 10 00 01 00 64 F7. Element enable (e1On..e4On, bits of one byte, notInPatch, pcParam 7F): keep a local byte starting at 0F and send the whole byte. Params with dumpArea 'none' are never in a dump. No acknowledgement; errors come back as F0 43 1n 35 7F 00 00 00 00 <err> F7 (see yamaha.errors). Receiving any voice param change makes the TG55 LCD jump to that edit page. Pace ~20 ms between messages (not specified by Yamaha). (3) DUMP FORMAT: F0 43 0n 7A bcHi bcLo 'LM  8103' 'VC' 14x00 memType memNum data... sum F7. Byte count = 26 + data length (7-bit halves): 1AWM 01 38 (184), 2AWM 02 31 (305), 4AWM 04 23 (547), drum 04 64 (612). Checksum = (128 - (sum of bytes from 'L' through last data byte) % 128) % 128. Data = mode byte (5/6/7; 10 = drum set -> treat as raw/unsupported), name x10, effect x5, common x21, element data 9 x N, then 112 x N element blocks. Keep a 521-byte canonical 4-element mirror (the schema's dumpOffset): parse a dump with N = mode-4 (5->1, 6->2, 7->4) by copying offsets 0-36, elementData 37+9e (+9 bytes), and elementBlock from 37+9N+112e into canonical 73+112e (+112); elements >= N keep their previous mirror bytes. Unmodelled bytes (reserves at canonical 26, 27, 99, 211, 323, 435) ride along from the last dump. Encodings: 'msb1' = 2 bytes [v>>7, v&7F]; 'signMag' as in yamaha.encodings; everything else one byte. (4) READ EDIT BUFFER (requestPatch): send F0 43 20 7A 4C 4D 20 20 38 31 30 33 56 43 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 7F 00 F7 and wait (~600 ms) for the next F0 43 0x 7A ... 'VC' dump; verify byte count and checksum; decode. If nothing arrives, the unit is probably in multi/demo mode or Device# off. SY55-Editor sends a harmless voice param change first (voice volume) to force voice edit; do that as a retry. (5) SEND EDIT BUFFER (sendPatch): build a dump from the mirror with N from values.mode, memType 7F, memNum 00; it is accepted in voice mode regardless of Bulk In Protect. Alternative: a burst of param changes (slower, ~450 messages). (6) READ STORED VOICE (requestProgram): same request with memType = bank.sysex.memoryType (00 internal, 02 preset) and memNum = prog (0-63). Does not change the playing voice. Per the manual, single-voice transmissions are labelled memType 7F / memNum 00, so match the reply on 'VC' only, not on memType/number. Card voices: not requestable -- select (programChange) then requestPatch. Slots 62/63 return a 612-byte drum dump: return {syx} + name only (values undefined). Name = data bytes 1-10. (7) WRITE STORED VOICE (writeProgram, internal only): send the voice dump with memType 00, memNum = prog. Requires Bulk In Protect OFF (else error 06 'MIDI Bulk Prot.'); optional: first send system param F0 43 1n 35 0F 00 00 07 00 00 F7 (Bulk Data Memory Protect off -- listed as receivable, untested). No ACK: wait >= 120 ms, then read the slot back and compare (sameProgram on modelled params). Refuse drum slots 62/63 and preset/card banks. (8) PROGRAM CHANGE: needs Program Change = direct: send Cn <bank.select.prefix> then Cn <prog + bank.select.offset> (122 internal, 123 card, 124 preset voices; 125/127 internal/preset multis with prog 64-79). It discards unsaved edits. (9) MULTIS/SYSTEM: 'MU' (186 bytes, memType 00/02/7F, memNum 0-15) and 'SY' (42 bytes) dumps use the same header/checksum; backupOnly, store raw. (10) PACING: Yamaha requires > ~100 ms between successive bulk dumps in either direction (use 120 ms), and after a dump before the next request. (11) decode(ev): the TG55 transmits no parameter changes for front-panel edits; only error messages and requested dumps arrive. An SY55 does transmit F0 43 1n 35 ... changes -- decode them by (G, S & 0x4F without element bits, P) with element = (S >> 4) & 3, wire = V1<<7 | V2, then signMag-decode. Ignore output-select value 7 (SY55 transmit marker).
uncertain: Wave number base: the manual gives 0-255 without saying whether 0 = wave 001. Treated as 0-based (0 = Piano ... 73 = Shaker): SY55-Editor sends the list index, and its SY55-captured init voice holds 45 = 'Tri', a typical init wave. Confirm by sending wave 0 and checking the TG55 display reads 'Piano'.

Effect parameter raw values: Yamaha's MIDI tables list params 1-3 with no range; the unit ranges are from the manual's effect chapter, but the raw-index -> unit tables in effectTypes come from SY55-Editor (third party). The generic fxParam1-3 params are 0-100 raw; values above a type's 'max' are probably clamped or ignored.

Reply labelling: the manual says 1-voice/1-multi transmissions carry memType = edit buffer and memNum 00, while 'all voice' transmissions carry the real memory type/number. Whether a request for internal voice n comes back as 7F/00 or 00/n is not stated; match replies by 'VC' only and serialise requests.

Edit-buffer request pre-conditions: the manual only says voice edit-buffer dumps are RECEIVED only in voice mode. SY55-Editor sends a voice param change before requesting 'to put the synth in edit mode' -- it may or may not be needed on a TG55.

Writing internal memory by bulk dump (memType 00 + memNum) is the manual's documented path ('memory type other than edit buffer is processed as internal') but it gives no acknowledgement; whether it also reloads the playing/edit voice is unknown. Error 06 is expected if Bulk In Protect is on; the system param 07 (Bulk Data Memory Protect) is listed as receivable by param change, which would let the driver turn protection off remotely -- untested.

Drum-set voices (mode 10, internal/preset 63-64) use a different 612-byte layout (61 x 9 key data, chart 3); not modelled. Writing a normal voice into those slots presumably fails with error 19 'Voice Type'.

Changing 'mode' (1/2/4 elements) by parameter change is listed as received (values 5-7), but what data new elements get and whether the unit accepts it from every screen is not documented. Re-request the edit buffer after changing it.

The channel-pressure section lists 'Pan Bias' as an aftertouch destination, but no pan-bias param exists in the voice tables (voice common bytes 10-11 = 'Reserve', n2 1A/1B undefined). Not modelled; those bytes are preserved from the last dump.
Filter 2 cannot be HPF (manual: 'HPF in Filter 1 only'), modelled max 1. SY55-Editor comments an HPF cutoff range of 0-114; the manual prints 0-127 for both.
Filter Mode value 2 is printed 'EGVA' (EG + velocity? / EG-VA); label kept as in the manual.
Pitch EG Range: manual '1:2, 2:1, 3:1/2 oct' read as 1 = 2 octaves, 2 = 1 octave, 3 = 1/2 octave (SY55-Editor agrees); value 0 undefined.
Level-scaling offsets (cutoff and output level) are '1-255: -127~+127' over 2 bytes; 128 = 0 (the init voice stores 01 00). Value 0 undefined.
Voice name range printed '20-127': read as 20h-127 (32-127, printable ASCII).
Direct program change mode: 'd = 119-127 ... program change occurs when next program change message received' is read as a two-message prefix scheme (Cn 7A, Cn pp). Not tested.
Pacing for parameter changes is not specified (only >100 ms between bulk dumps). 20 ms is a guess; drop to 10 ms if it keeps up.
Device# 'all': the manual says transmission then uses device 1; reception on all numbers is inferred from the setting's name.

SY55 compatibility: the TG55 manual's notes (output select value 7 on SY55-transmitted param changes, 0 in SY55 dumps) imply the same format; SY55-Editor works on an SY55 with exactly these addresses. The TG55-only 'Output Select' (voice common 21h) is the only known functional difference.
